newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on heavy overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange in active trading on Thursday, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,490 yuan ($2,591) per tonne, losing 270 yuan. It opened at 21,360 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 21,300 and a high of 21,500.
February fell 220 to 21,490, March 260 to 21,430, April 260 to 21,440, June 290 to 21,480 and July 150 to 21,600.
Combined volume rose heavily to 46,230 tonnes from 14,560.
Copper opened sharply lower but buying at low levels pushed prices upwards for most of the session.

Traders said falls on the LME triggered panic selling at the beginning of the session from investors who do not want to hold positions over the lunar new year holday, but short-covering and fresh buying at low levels kept it from dropping further.
"Firm spot prices triggered strong short-covering and fresh buying," one trader added.
Spot copper is around 21,300 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
"Copper is likely to fluctuate tommorrow because many investors are eager to liquidate their positions on the last trading day before the long holiday," a second trader said.
